formation.explanation: A leader admits proposals subject to membership, transfer and configuration guards, assigns term/index and replicates. Followers validate previous log identity and preserve committed prefixes. Append responses and self support wait for persistence. Current-term leader consumes tracked voter matches via majority or both joint majorities; a matching current-term quorum endpoint advances commitment. Append/heartbeat propagate commitment, and Ready dispatches bounded committed prefixes to caller application. Heartbeat responses also restore replication flow after losses; compaction can require snapshot catch-up.

context.explanation: Eligible followers campaign after logical timeout or explicit request, with unapplied committed configuration and pending-snapshot guards. Vote freshness and term/vote rules constrain support; persisted self and remote votes feed current voter quorums. Pre-vote probes without term change. Winning installs leader state and an empty current-term entry. Higher terms, same-term leader traffic to candidates and optional quorum loss change role; reset clears progress, vote tally, read quorum state and transfer while preserving log decisions. Transfer catches up a voter then requests election; proposals pause and timeout aborts transfer. Lower-term network work is rejected or answered with current term; old storage acknowledgments have separate entry/snapshot handling.

connection.explanation: Authority selects whose support can form decisions, but committed history survives authority changes. Log freshness carries prior decisions into elections; current-term commitment qualifies deferred read processing. Configuration application changes both quorum aggregation and election eligibility, and can itself advance commitment using retained matches. Recovery reinstalls history and eligibility. Storage responses are term-filtered for overwrite-sensitive entries, whereas committed snapshot/application progress survives term transitions. Read quorum contexts reset on role change; the separate pre-first-commit request queue requires further lifecycle investigation. Automatic joint exit is attempted from applied progress; a transfer-rejected attempt is not retried by transfer timeout itself. Later application or leadership change may supply a new attempt.

grounding.derivation: ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit specifies that raft transitions out automatically by proposing a zero change, whereas JointExplicit assigns that proposal to the application. tracker.Config.AutoLeave repeats that ownership when possible. appliedTo implements the automatic proposal and documents transfer rejection plus an expected later advance. Generic proposal retry duties do not transfer this internal automatic task to the caller. The responsibility is eventual continuation under available quorums, not completion after a fixed number of ticks.
grounding.applicability: Actual committed/applied implicit transition and fully serviced stable-leader suffix after a finite failed transfer. A violation requires a closed non-progress execution suffix or equivalently sourced proof that required future triggers cannot occur, beyond finite non-completion.
alternatives: A successful leadership change or later applied ordinary entry can initiate exit; those rescue paths do not establish automatic continuation in a stable idle workload.

grounding.derivation: Ready.ReadStates and RawNode.ReadIndex explicitly authorize linearizable local reads once applied is beyond the returned index. For a register with completed B preceding read invocation and no later writes, linearizability requires B. Ready.MustSync explicitly permits non-durable writes when false, and the producer does not sync commit-only HardState changes. Crash recovery from a durable log ahead of the last synchronized commit therefore belongs to the interface scope. Request-loss permission cannot authorize an incorrect completed read.
grounding.applicability: Application and persistence contracts are met in the same crash/restart history; the predicate compares actual read output to a prior completed register write using independent operation identity.
alternatives: Delaying reads until all committed replay completes is a stronger caller policy than the returned-index condition; the fixed driver uses the documented index condition conservatively.
